transcript:
[00:00] Maya (AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining, we will run about an hour, agenda is packaging, auth, network, and UAT playbook. quick intros?
[00:18] Priya (Head of Platform): hi, Priya here, I own platform and infra at AcornLoop, we'll be the listing owners.
[00:25] Samir (Cloud Architect): Samir, cloud architect, I'll handle the VPC and networking side.
[00:30] Janelle (PM): Janelle on product, interested in the dev experience for customers.
[00:36] Maya: awesome, diego from our side will do the tech deep dive.
[00:40] Diego (SE): hi all, quick note: apologies if auto-transcript spits odd words, I talk fast.
[00:46] Maya: ok first slide, packaging checklist — this is our standard marketplace listing requirements, helm package, OCI images, image scanning, and attestation.
[00:58] Priya: can you call out what you mean by attestation? we've got an internal SBOM process.
[01:05] Diego: sure, attestation here is basically signed provenance metadata, we ask for image digest and a simple SBOM link. it's not prescriptive, just requires we can validate the image matches the listing. sometimes CT logs or Cosign are used.
[01:22] Samir: we run ECR in account A and a shared registry in account B, so we need guidance on registry permissions and pull policy.
[01:30] Maya: good call — our recommended pattern is pull from a customer-managed registry with a read-only role for the runtime; we'll include example IAM policies in the checklist.
[01:41] Janelle: what about upgrades? automatic chart updates will break canaries if not pinned.
[01:46] Diego: we recommend pinning image digests in values.yaml and using canary images for rollouts. Redwood supports model pinning on the deployment side too — sorry that sounds like overloading terms, by model pinning I mean image/model version pinning.
[01:59] Maya: moving to authz: customers often ask whether they should embed SSO inside the listing or use marketplace SSO passthrough. thoughts?
[02:10] Priya: we need to centralize auth; security wants SAML with our IdP and SCIM for user sync. we don't want per-tenant credentials embedded.
[02:19] Diego: for private deployments we do a couple patterns: 1) SSO passthrough where the marketplace acts as an identity broker, or 2) SSO redirect handled by the runtime inside the customer's VPC. both okay, depends on your compliance.
[02:34] Samir: technically we prefer option 2, because we can preserve session cookies and IAM mapping internally. but we need a clear handshake for trust — certs, JWKS endpoints etc.
[02:45] Maya: note — customers request SAML and OIDC; we should support both. Diego, can we produce a sample SAML metadata and OIDC config to share?
[02:53] Diego: yes, will add a sample metadata.xml and an OIDC discovery doc to the repo.
[02:58] Janelle: side question — what does RBAC look like inside the listing? can we map marketplace roles to internal RBAC?
[03:07] Diego: short answer: yes. we provide role mapping hooks. the simplest pattern is to accept a signed assertion from the marketplace with role claims, then map to k8s RBAC or internal app roles. but you'll have to define the canonical claims.
[03:25] Priya: security will want audit logs — how are those surfaced?
[03:30] Maya: Redwood emits audit logs to customer endpoints or can push to a syslog/S3 that you control. we also provide token-level tracing in the console.
[03:40] Samir: networking question: will the listing require VPC peering, or can we use private endpoints? we have some regions where peering isn't allowed.
[03:50] Diego: two supported connectivity patterns — classic VPC peering with restricted CIDR ranges, or private-service-endpoints (private link) where the runtime sits in a shared services VPC. peering is simpler but not always available.
[04:05] Samir: ok, that matches constraints. we'll probably go private endpoint in regions that disallow peering. any static egress IPs to whitelist?
[04:13] Maya: yes we can provide a list of egress ranges per region; we'll need to coordinate before UAT.
[04:20] Diego: note: sometimes our auto-transcript shows "egress ranges" as "egress rangers" so ignore that.
[04:25] Janelle: KMS — we use a managed KMS with strict rotation. what's the integration surface?
[04:31] Diego: options: Redwood-managed KMS (not ideal for enterprise), or customer-managed keys via external KMS/HSM. For marketplace you can supply an envelope key and the runtime will use KMS APIs to unwrap secrets at start. we'll document the exact calls (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, GCP CMEK).
[04:50] Priya: will Redwood store any plaintext secrets? we need zero-retention of plaintext.
[04:55] Maya: default is zero retention; we only cache ephemeral tokens in memory. persistent secrets are stored encrypted with the customer KMS or left in customer secret store via CSI driver.
[05:07] Samir: ok good. next, packaging constraints — we have an init container that performs customer-specific bootstrap, does that break marketplace guardrails?
[05:16] Diego: init containers are fine, but we ask that they run unprivileged. no hostNetwork, no hostPath writes beyond /tmp sandbox. we will flag privileged containers during approval.
[05:28] Priya: scanning — do you do automated vulnerability scans during listing?
[05:32] Maya: we run an image scan and expect a remediation plan for criticals; we can accept a timeline for fixes for medium severity. we'll add the scan report to the listing metadata.
[05:45] Janelle: billing/ metering — how does the marketplace meter usage? do we need an SDK call?
[05:51] Diego: Redwood offers a metering endpoint you can call for usage events; alternatively if listing in a cloud marketplace they may provide a billing hook. we'll share an example emitter (node/python) for token/seat usage.
[06:05] Priya: latency concerns — customers may push models that require GPU. do marketplace listings support specifying resource profiles?
[06:13] Maya: yes the listing can declare resource profiles (cpu/cpu/ accelerator types), and our control plane will route to appropriate instance types. For Dedicated or Hosted variants the routing differs; we'll include recommended profiles.
[06:28] Samir: slightly off-topic: do you support quantized models and how does that affect the packaging?
[06:33] Diego: quantized models are supported but you should include the quantization metadata and test vectors. we recommend a small eval set so we can validate inference correctness during onboarding.
[06:45] Maya: ok let's pivot to UAT/connectivity playbook — Diego?
[06:49] Diego: UAT steps: 1) review packaging checklist 2) deploy in a staging account with sample values.yaml 3) run connectivity script (we have a small k8s job that checks API, metrics, and KMS unwrap) 4) execute smoke test with a canned prompt/eval 5) capture logs and scan report and share.
[07:12] Samir: the connectivity script will need outbound to your endpoints — can you provide fqdn and ip ranges for staging?
[07:20] Maya: yes, staging endpoints are different from production; we'll provide them in the checklist. note production egress ranges will be longer lived.
[07:29] Janelle: any gotchas we should watch for in Azure region deployments?
[07:34] Diego: watch for ACR private link and dns resolution for private endpoints; sometimes customers miss /etc/hosts entries for cluster DNS. we'll provide a troubleshooting doc.
[07:45] Priya: compliance question — do you require us to sign a data processing addendum for marketplace listing?
[07:52] Maya: yes enterprise accounts will sign DPA and we support contractual clauses for data residency. we'll share our standard DPA and SOC2 docs.
[08:01] Samir: security wants the option of in-transit mTLS between runtime and our services. is that supported?
[08:08] Diego: yes we support mTLS via cert exchange and mutual auth. we'll provide a cert rotation guide; if you're using a CA internally we can integrate with that.
[08:19] Priya: when you say certificate rotation guide, is there automation or it's manual?
[08:24] Diego: we provide both: an automated cert-renew job that integrates with cert-manager, or manual rotation steps if you prefer.
[08:33] Maya: ok, quick poll — does AcornLoop want marketplace listing to be fully self-service or do you prefer a co-managed onboarding?
[08:41] Priya: co-managed to start, because we want to validate security posture first.
[08:45] Janelle: agree — we'll move to self-serve after the first two customers are onboarded.
[08:50] Diego: noted. next, approval workflow — we require certain metadata for listing: description, supported resource profiles, SBOM link, scan report, contact, and support SLA.
[09:03] Maya: on support SLA — customers sometimes propose 24/7 for platform emergencies. what's typical?
[09:10] Janelle: for marketplace customers we'd start with business hours and an escalation path; may move to 24/7 for enterprise customers.
[09:16] Diego: our recommended default is 8x5 with extended pager for severity 1. we can negotiate enterprise SLAs separately.
[09:25] Priya: action on us: we'll map our support levels and send an initial proposal.
[09:29] Maya: great. anything on the packaging side we missed?
[09:33] Samir: one more network thing — NAT gateways are expensive; can we use a shared egress ENI?
[09:38] Diego: yes patterns vary; we document shared NAT, egress NAT gateway pools, and proxy patterns in the playbook. we'll include cost notes.
[09:47] Janelle: can we surface telemetry to our observability stack? we use Datadog and Grafana.
[09:52] Maya: yes we can push traces/metrics via OTLP and logs via a forwarder; integration samples will be in the repo.
[09:59] Priya: curious about rollout — do you support canary routing per tenant?
[10:05] Diego: yes, our runtime supports canaries and traffic-splitting by tenant or route. we recommend a 10/90 canary window and health-check probes.
[10:14] Maya: ok we're about 10 minutes in, but this is a lot; maybe we should timebox further sections. we'll jump to open risks.
[10:22] Diego: risk 1: image scanning failures delaying listing. mitigation: agreed remediation SLA.
[10:27] Priya: risk 2: network egress restrictions in gov regions. mitigation: private endpoint pattern.
[10:33] Samir: risk 3: SSO mapping divergence — mitigation: define canonical claims and test mapping in UAT.
[10:40] Janelle: risk 4: billing mismatch — mitigation: run pilot with metering hooks and reconcile events.
[10:46] Maya: perfect. can we list owners for each risk briefly?
[10:52] Diego: I'll own image scan remediation flow docs.
[10:55] Priya: I'll own region compliance and lists.
[10:58] Samir: I own network test and egress list.
[11:02] Maya: next steps recap: I will send packaging checklist; Diego will share SAML/OIDC samples and connectivity script; Priya and Samir will send diagrams.
[11:12] Janelle: can we get an estimate of time to go from listing to first customer?
[11:17] Maya: typical co-managed onboarding is 3-6 weeks depending on security review and scans.
[11:23] Priya: acceptable.
[11:25] Diego: quick demo snippet — (slight pause) I'm going to share my screen, but transcript may drop.
[11:35] [screen share noises, brief pause]
[11:45] Diego: here is the sample values.yaml — note image: "registry.acornloop.io/acornloop/service@sha256:..." pinned digest, and service account role with read-only ECR access.
[11:58] Samir: that looks good. what about secrets? where do we reference KMS key ARN?
[12:04] Diego: values.yaml has kmsKeyArn and a boolean useExternalKms — if true, runtime expects to call your KMS to unwrap. we'll document the exact permissions.
[12:16] Janelle: will you accept a vault CSI driver mount instead of in-cluster secrets?
[12:22] Diego: yes CSI is fine; just document and test during UAT.
[12:28] Priya: any required labels or annotations for marketplace telemetry?
[12:33] Maya: annotate with marketplace.meta.* keys; we'll publish exact annotation schema.
[12:40] Samir: SLA on image scanning results — do you block listing on critical vuln?
[12:45] Diego: criticals must be remediated before GA; for medium we can accept a plan with timeline.
[12:53] Janelle: ok, timeline planning: we aim to start pilot in mid-december, is that feasible?
[12:59] Maya: given current time, yes but dependent on scan results and security review. propose we set internal checkpoint 2026-11-30 to confirm.
[13:08] Priya: we'll target that.
[13:11] Diego: small note — the transcript sometimes writes "RV K S" for KMS, so you'll see weird tokens.
[13:16] Maya: lol noted. any more open questions from the AcornLoop team?
[13:21] Priya: what's the approval SLA from Redwood side after we submit package?
[13:25] Maya: review turnaround is typically 4 business days for packaging + scan verification, longer if issues found.
[13:32] Samir: can we get preflight checks as a CI job? we'd like to run the same checks before submission.
[13:39] Diego: yes we'll provide a preflight GH action you can include in CI. it runs the image scan, checks values.yaml schema, and ensures required annotations present.
[13:51] Janelle: excellent. any cross-account permission needs?
[13:55] Diego: none required for preflight; for runtime tests you might grant a read-only execution role. we'll detail minimal perms.
[14:05] Priya: ok last concern — data residency for EU customers. listings sometimes route to multi-region infra; can we pin region?
[14:13] Maya: yes marketplace listing can declare region constraints and the control plane will honor pinned deployment region for those tenants.
[14:21] Samir: that is critical for our customers.
[14:25] Maya: wrapping up — recap and owners (see actions). we'll schedule the follow-up SSO deep dive with your security person next week.
[14:36] Priya: thanks all, appreciate the thoroughness.
[14:39] Maya: thanks team. I'll send notes and the checklist after the call.
[14:44] Janelle: bye everyone.
[14:46] [call end — auto transcript truncated, final timestamps may be approximate]
